study.title: Discretionary Tax Changes and the Macroeconomy: New Narrative Evidence from the United Kingdom

audit.engine: anomalyco/opencode (ReproAI) - DeepSeek V4 Flash via uniGPT
audit.headline_numbers_note: Corroborated via published human reproduction (I4R DP132) and internal-consistency checks; NOT independently recomputed because raw ICPSR data could not be downloaded (Cloudflare on OpenICPSR /download + ICPSR deposit login wall).
audit.verdict_note: Package is complete and an independent published reproduction reproduced all VAR tables/figures exactly; I agree it is computationally reproducible. My failure to recompute is an access-layer limitation, not a package defect.
audit.independent_recompute_reason: raw quarterly UK macro data + Cloyne's constructed narrative tax-shock series live only in the inaccessible ICPSR package

headline_claims.claim: 1%-of-GDP tax cut raises UK GDP ~0.6% on impact
peak GDP response ~2.5% over ~3 years (10-11 quarters)
peak comparable to Romer & Romer (2010) US (~2.5 at 10-11 qtrs)

internal_consistency_checks.detail: I4R DP132 Table 1 reproduction numbers: z=coef/SE and 95% CI=coef +/- 1.96*SE recompute within rounding for author-code and Stata columns; cross-source abstract (0.6/2.5) matches reproduction (0.599/2.458).

findings.title: Raw replication data effectively inaccessible for automated third-party verification
Author's original MATLAB bootstrap samples residuals non-jointly across the VAR block, understating the peak-response SE (0.797 vs 1.012 with joint resampling)
Headline p-values not emitted by code; reconstructed as bootstrap share-below-zero (effectively one-sided)
Reproduction requires proprietary MATLAB + EViews; not runnable open-source-only
